# Delegation tiers on each host

| Tier | Role | Claude Code | Codex |
|---|---|---|---|
| `judge` | plan, rule, review, diagnose | `claude-opus-5-5`, effort `medium` | `gpt-6.1-sol`, effort `medium` |
| `execute` | bulk reading, work pinned by a spec or oracle | `claude-sonnet-5-5`, default effort | `gpt-6.1-sol`, effort `low` |
| `routine` | run, triage, summarise, mechanical edits | `claude-haiku-5-5`, default effort | `gpt-6-luna`, default effort |

`judge` is the main session: no definition, never spawned. Its row is the
expected setting for the session, which the skill can't set.

## Starting a tier

Start a tier only after `check.py open`. Its task is one of the two loader lines `open`
prints, not the brief's text; `brief` prints the recorded brief and refuses if it changed:

- `task:`, for an agent defined with the tier's instructions:

      Run `python3 <absolute skill-dir>/scripts/check.py --root <absolute worktree root> brief --delegation <id>` and follow the brief it prints exactly.

- `task with instructions:`, for any other subagent. It adds `--with-instructions`, so
  `brief` prints the tier's instructions (under "Tier instructions" below) first.

Tools don't expand shell syntax, so never pass `$(cat ...)` or a bare path as the task.

### Claude Code

Use the Agent tool with `subagent_type` set to the tier's agent:

- `execute`: `delegation:execute`
- `routine`: `delegation:routine`

Never pass `model` or `effort`: the generated definition sets them, and a per-call
value overrides it. The environment overrides definitions too: `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL`
sets every agent's effort, and `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE` with
`CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` forces every subagent's model. If either is set, the table
doesn't hold; say so once.

If the `delegation:<tier>` agents aren't available, start a general-purpose subagent with the
`task with instructions:` line as its prompt, and pass `model` as the tier's alias below
(this fallback is the only case that passes `model`). Never pass `effort`; it stays at the
default.

- `execute`: `model` = `sonnet`
- `routine`: `model` = `haiku`

### Codex (route: spawn)

The delegation skill is your explicit instruction to spawn these subagents.

Codex plugins can't ship agent definitions, so spawn the default subagent with the
tier's model and effort. Call `spawn_agent` with:

- `task_name`: lowercase letters, digits and underscores only (Codex rejects anything else), such as the id lowercased with `-` and `.` as `_`
- `fork_turns`: `"none"`, always. A forked child inherits your context, which defeats delegation.
- `model` and `reasoning_effort`: the tier's values below, given explicitly
- `message`: the `task with instructions:` line that `open` printed

Per tier:

- `execute`: `model`: `"gpt-6.1-sol"`, `reasoning_effort`: `"low"`
- `routine`: `model`: `"gpt-6-luna"`, omit `reasoning_effort` (the model's default)

If `spawn_agent` rejects `model` or `reasoning_effort`, spawn without them and with the
same `message`: same model, default effort.

## Tier instructions

Each tier's generated instructions, verbatim. A Claude Code tier agent already has them;
`brief --with-instructions` prints them for any other subagent, before the brief.

### `execute`

````text
You are the `execute` tier of a delegation pod. The brief is your whole task.
- If your task is a `check.py brief` command, run it first and follow the brief it prints. If it exits non-zero, stop and report its stderr.
- Follow the brief. Write only what its "May write" field permits; a reader writes nothing.
- For single-writer resources and anything under "Must not write", return proposed changes instead of editing.
- Trust the brief's "Settled" facts; don't reread sources to verify them. If what you see contradicts one, report it under Surprises instead of working around it.
- "Inputs" bound your reading. Read beyond them only when blocked, and list what you read and why under Surprises.
- Run validators only through the brief's `check.py run` command. Cite a result as `[checked: <id>]` only when it printed PASS and not "unstable"; otherwise use `[cited: <refs>]` or `[asserted]`.
- When stuck, stop and report what you tried and your evidence. Don't guess.
- Return exactly the brief's return format, within its return cap.
````
